articles.headline: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama not interested in promoting betting sites
articles.description: Spurs star Victor Wembanyama said Thursday that he isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Count Spurs star Victor Wembanyama as one of the professional athletes that isn't interested in promoting sports betting sites.

The Frenchman expressed his view on the subject Thursday after a training camp workout.

"Absolutely not," Wembanyama said when asked if he'd ever consider promoting a sports betting website. "I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was subsequently asked how he makes decisions about which brands to promote.

"In the past, there was a dimension of money," he said. "Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not [in line with] my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. Obviously, we earn millions and millions. This is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

Several of Wembanyama's NBA peers currently promote sportsbooks and prediction platforms, including LeBron James, who moved from DraftKings to Polymarket in September, Kevin Durant (FanDuel), who is also an investor in Kalshi and Giannis Antetokounmpo, who became a shareholder at Kalshi back in February.

"The internet is full of opinions," Antetokounmpo wrote in a since-deleted post on X, announcing the move. "I decided it was time to make some of my own. Today, I'm joining Kalshi as a shareholder."

Three-time MVP Nikola Jokic, in 2023, became the first brand ambassador of Superbet in Serbia.

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement treats sports betting operators and prediction markets the same when it comes down to player partnerships. Players aren't allowed to promote betting on any market related to the NBA. But they are allowed to endorse and hold de minimis equity investments in sports betting companies with some restrictions.

Wembanyama, meanwhile, enters his fourth season in the league coming off San Antonio's first appearance in the NBA Finals since 2014. The two-time All-Star last season became the first player to unanimously win NBA Defensive Player of the Year after leading the league in blocks for the third-consecutive season.

Wembanyama, 22, finished third last season in voting for NBA MVP.

articles.headline: Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more
articles.description: Tuesday's news that the Premier League found Man City guilty of 100-plus charges of breaking financial rules is a landmark moment. But what comes next: what punishments are on the table, and how does the appeals process work?
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules is a landmark moment in global sport.

City continues to assert their innocence and have signaled their intention to appeal before Friday's deadline. But the Independent Commission's verdict could hardly have been more damning, accusing the club of "sham" contracts involving its Abu Dhabi owners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" that contributed to inflating revenues and reducing costs by over £900 million. Witnesses in City's defense were accused of dishonesty, and the club was found to have "clearly intended to circumvent" Premier League rules.

The breaches relate specifically to a nine-year period (2009-18), but the shockwaves permeate far beyond. Pep Guardiola's trophy-laden legacy is in doubt. The Premier League's reputation and viability is in the balance. Rivals may seek retribution through compensation claims, triggering challenges that could last for years.

Meanwhile, City's punishment is yet to be determined. Under Section W, Rule 54 of the Premier League's Handbook, they are facing a punishment ranging from a reprimand to expulsion. There could be a fine, a points deduction and a transfer ban.

City's aggressive protestations of innocence only contribute to the widespread uncertainty and reduces the likelihood of all parties coming together to reach agreement on a settlement for the time being. Beyond that, the legal complexities are vast.

ESPN has spoken with one of the United Kingdom's leading law firms, Howard Kennedy, in pursuit of clarity. Partners Kyle Phillips and Lois Langton head the firm's sports group, with Phillips specializing in business crime and regulatory process. On Thursday, the pair talked with ESPN's James Olley to answer some basic questions and follow-ups about what this all means and what's next.

Editor's Note: This interview has been edited for clarity and length.

How would you characterize the commission's findings?

Kyle Phillips: I think it's worse than many people expected. The words that were used by the commission in the findings report, caveated with the fact it's very difficult to read because a lot of it is redacted and there's no evidence or appendices that they keep referring to, but the language that they use is very strong.

"Sham" is one point. You've got the disguised payments, sorry -- the "disguised funding scheme," overstating commercial revenue, the amounts involved ... it is all quite shocking. And it is quite a strong statement to say that you find the witness evidence that was given to be "dishonest" -- a powerful word in any decision.

In any regulatory proceedings, it takes a lot for them to use that word.

How deliberate is this language? Are they effectively trying to preempt or dissuade an appeal?

articles.headline: Johnson and Glenn match wits once again as the Bears host the Jets in Week 4
articles.description: — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Ben Johnson's time in Detroit — a formative experience that led to his current job as coach of the Chicago Bears — was shaped in part by going against Aaron Glenn's defense in practice with the Lions.


              Johnson remembers it well.


              “He certainly lights a fire under you," he said. “I still remember to this day being next to him in training camp, and you can hear him. You can hear him. And when the defense makes a play, he lets you know."


              Johnson goes up against Glenn once again on Sunday when the Bears host the New York Jets. Glenn took over in New York in January 2025, right after Johnson was hired by Chicago.


              Johnson, 40, was the offensive coordinator for Detroit while Glenn, 54, was the defensive coordinator with the Lions. Glenn faced their former boss last weekend, losing to 31-24 to Dan Campbell's Lions in Detroit.


              Glenn recalled planning for practice with Johnson in one of their first meetings after he took over the offense.


              “Just having those conversations and seeing how he put things together, and then just talking offensive and defensive football was good to have,” Glenn said. "But the one thing, we were so competitive in move-the-ball situations on how we wanted to beat each other, but it made both of us better, I will say that. He’s a damn good coach.”


              Glenn and New York are preparing for a Chicago team with an uncertain situation at quarterback, at least publicly. Caleb Williams is rehabbing a right hamstring injury. Case Keenum passed for two touchdowns in Monday night's win over Philadelphia, but Johnson hasn't identified the starter for the matchup with the Jets.


              Chicago also could go with Tyson Bagent, who emerged from the NFL’s concussion protocol on Sunday.


              Whoever gets the call for the Bears will face an improved Jets defense, directed by Glenn, who was a defensive back in the NFL for 15 seasons.


              “You can see how he played the game as a player has translated to how he coaches, and his guys take that same identity as well,” Johnson said. "Like I said, a ton of respect for him and he’s a heck of a competitor.” 


              Need to know
              New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago (2-1).

              Series record: Bears lead 9-4.

articles.headline: Texans host the Cowboys seeking their first win after an 0-3 start
articles.description: — After a second straight 0-3 start to the season, any win would be huge for the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- — After a second straight 0-3 start to the season, any win would be huge for the Houston Texans.


              But getting that elusive first win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday would certainly mean a little something extra.


              “We know how big this game is and how much it means to our fans here in the city of Houston,” coach DeMeco Ryans said. “We have to play well to give our fans what they’ve been searching for and that’s that first win and I’m excited.”


              These teams don’t play very often, with Sunday being just the eighth all-time meeting, making these rare matchups a big deal in the state.


              The Cowboys lead the series 4-3, but Houston has won two of the past three meetings, including a 34-10 victory in Arlington, Texas, in the most recent matchup in 2024. And diehard Texans fans still fondly remember when Houston got its first-ever win as a franchise with a 19-10 triumph over Dallas in 2002.


              Now in their 25th season, Sunday’s game will be an anniversary celebration featuring a halftime ceremony honoring Texans greats including Hall of Famer Andre Johnson, J.J. Watt, Arian Foster, DeAndre Hopkins, Brian Cushing and Billy Miller along with former coach Gary Kubiak.


              Houston defensive end Will Anderson is trying to stay focused this week despite all the hoopla surrounding the game.


              “The biggest thing (is) how much more can we focus in on just doing your job and just being where you’re supposed to be and doing what you’re supposed to do,” he said. “Then when we get to the game, we can worry about the rivalry in Texas and stuff like that.”


              While the Texans are one of five winless NFL teams this season, the Cowboys year hasn’t gone much better. Dallas is 1-2 after a 34-31 loss to Baltimore on a last-second field goal last week.


              It’s a game that led to owner Jerry Jones saying he believes errors in game management by his coaching staff in the final seconds cost his team the win.


              Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer knows better than to underestimate the Texans despite another awful start.


              “We know that we want to focus on us, but clearly when you watch them play, they’re not a 0-3 team,” he said. “Their record says they’re 0-3, but hard pressed to find a better defense than this front.”

articles.headline: Brock Purdy and the 49ers prepare for a tough test against the Broncos defense
articles.description: — Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers have been in peak form early this season.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — Brock Purdy and the San Francisco 49ers have been in peak form early this season.


              The Niners lead the league in yards per play and success rate, have limited negative plays and rank second in the league in scoring to fuel a 3-0 start. That unit will get its toughest test yet on Sunday when the 49ers host the Denver Broncos (2-1) and one of the league's best defenses under coordinator Vance Joseph.


              “Vance is one of the toughest guys just because he can do anything,” San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan said. "It’s not a surprise they were one of the best defenses in the league last year.”


              But no offense is operating like the 49ers early this season with the team averaging 32.7 points per game and scoring touchdowns on nearly half of their possessions.


              While the big plays such as the 82-yard hook-and-ladder touchdown last week against Arizona get the highlights, the key has been avoiding negative plays. 


              The offense has gone 11 straight quarters without a turnover and has lost yardage on just four plays from scrimmage all season — the fewest through three games since at least 2000.


              The 49ers are the first team in 12 years to allow no sacks through three games as Purdy's elusiveness and strong play from the offense line have frustrated the opposition.


              “Obviously, the play calling, the boys up front, the receivers being on top of making sure they’re running the right routes and getting the ball out on time and stuff on our end at quarterback. So, it’s a unit thing,” Purdy said about the lack of sacks. “It takes everybody. Obviously it starts with the boys up front too, though. They’re playing their butt off right now.”


              The Broncos offer a formidable challenge. They lead the NFL with 139 sacks since the start of the 2024 season — 27 more than the next best team — and know they need to get pressure on Purdy to have a chance Sunday.


              That's not as easy as it sounds. 


              “He’s playing at a real high level, very decisive," coach Sean Payton said. "He’s through his progressions fast. Kyle and those guys have done a great job, whether he’s under center or in the gun. The mix of run, play pass and drop back is impressive. You see in three weeks, not only no sacks, first in third down, first in red zone, very efficient. He’s making all the throws.”

articles.headline: Allen seeks to put sloppy play behind him as Bills host turnover-prone Maye and the Patriots
articles.description: — Win or lose, Josh Allen has displayed a consistent knack for putting a sloppy performance behind him.
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- — Win or lose, Josh Allen has displayed a consistent knack for putting a sloppy performance behind him.


              It’s reflected in the smile and cheery “How’s everybody doing?” greeting the Bills quarterback opens each of his weekly news conferences with. And it bears out in the numbers: the ninth-year player has never lost more than two straight starts and holds a 30-8 record following a loss.


              “He embodies competitive stamina,” coach Joe Brady said on Wednesday after Allen pulled out a 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday despite committing three of Buffalo’s five turnovers. “The fact that we can win that game with all those circumstances shows that mentality, his personality.”


              It’s a resilient quality the Bills (3-0) can draw upon in renewing their divisional rivalry by hosting New England (1-2) on Sunday.


              Drake Maye and the Patriots are seeking to adopt a similar approach following a shaky September.


              A season after going 14-3 and leading New England to the Super Bowl, Maye's opened his third season with one touchdown pass versus six interceptions and a lost fumble. 


              The troubles go back to the start of the playoffs, with Maye committing a combined 15 turnovers (10 interceptions, five fumbles).


              Coach Mike Vrabel used a golf analogy to identify what might be Maye's issues.


              “Sometimes we’re so focused on it that we try to choke the life out of the golf club. And we’re squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways,” he said. “We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football.”


              Maye threw interceptions on three consecutive drives to close a 13-10 season-opening loss at Seattle. And following a 20-3 win versus Pittsburgh in which the New England's defense accounted for a TD, he threw two interceptions and lost a fumble in a 35-6 loss at Jacksonville.


              “You’ve got to lean on your faith (in God),” Maye said. “I know it’s not where we wanted to be, and not where we want to start. But it’s how you fight back, respond and know that this league’s not always sunshine and rainbows.”


              The Patriots’ 29 points scored on 30 drives represents the NFL's lowest rate of conversion through three games of a season since the 2021 New York Jets.


              Buffalo leads the NFL, averaging 33.7 points per outing. The Bills have an opportunity to open a three-game lead on New England a season after the Patriots ended Buffalo’s five-year run of AFC East titles.


              Allen said it’s too early to worry about playoff seeding, with his prime focus on cleaning up offensive mistakes. 


              He also extended support to Maye.


              “Listen, Drake’s a smart kid. Extremely talented,” Allen said. “I’ve got a lot of respect for him and what he’s been able to do in his early career. He’ll find a way out of it.”

articles.headline: Commanders' Jayden Daniels says he's taking injury day by day
articles.description: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels said Thursday he has no concerns about reinjuring his left elbow and is "taking it day by day" on the possibility of starting against the Colts on Sunday in London.
articles.body:
HERTFORDSHIRE, England -- Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels said he doesn't have any concern about potentially reinjuring his dislocated left elbow once he returns to playing.

"That's what the brace is for," he said Thursday. "If I had that concern, I would have gotten surgery."

Daniels was a limited participant in practice for the second consecutive day Thursday at the five-star luxury resort where the Commanders (1-2) are staying ahead of Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts (1-2).

But it remains uncertain whether Daniels will play. If not, then Marcus Mariota will make a second consecutive start. When asked if he was surprised to even be back on the field so soon after a second dislocation, Daniels said, with a smile, "What do you think?"

Then he said, "I'm not surprised. Everything I went through, everybody said I would be good to go if I'm able to be out there Sunday. But I'm taking it day by day."

Daniels dislocated his left arm in a Week 2 loss at Dallas, the second time he suffered that injury to his non-throwing arm. He dislocated it in Week 9 last season, then aggravated it five weeks later at Minnesota. Washington decided to then shut him down for the rest of the season.

After his latest injury, Daniels visited multiple specialists in New York and Los Angeles. Multiple experts in this field told ESPN that it's rare for someone to have surgery after a first dislocation because the rate of recurrence is between 1% and 2%. But the percentage shoots up after a second one -- depending on how much the ligaments loosened.

But the specialists did not recommend surgery; Daniels also just wanted to play.

"I love playing football, I get paid to play football," Daniels said. "Everybody is hurting. I just feel for me being a leader, go out there and give it my shot to go out and play and obviously protect myself. I just love football and have a passion for it."

Surgery could be an option after the season -- Daniels said he would listen to what doctors say at the time before making any decision. If he comes back Sunday or even the following week against the New York Giants, he would have returned quicker than he did the first time. However, he will be wearing a different brace -- one that keeps his elbow slightly bent to prevent another dislocation.

Daniels said he's not worried about another dislocation or possible long-term damage.

"Obviously you have those conversations with people I need to have those conversations with. If the surgery was needed to be ASAP, then I've got to do what's best for me. We had those conversations. I was blessed enough to go back out there on the practice field ... I'm not really concerned at this moment."

articles.headline: Why Matthew Stafford made a cameo in Taylor Swift's 'Patient Zero' music video
articles.description: Why, yes, that was Matthew Stafford. Here's why all signs pointed to the reigning NFL MVP's music video cameo.
articles.body:
Never let it be said Matthew Stafford lacks range.

If you find yourself watching Taylor Swift's recently debuted music video for "Patient Zero" and see someone who happens to bear a striking resemblance to the Los Angeles Rams quarterback, that's because it is said quarterback.

In the video, which also stars actors Colin Farrell, Dakota Johnson and Cara Delevingne, the Super Bowl LVI champion and reigning NFL MVP makes a cameo at a black-tie affair alongside his wife, Kelly Stafford. Stafford's not the only athlete in the scene, as former Los Angeles Kings center and two-time Stanley Cup champion Jarret Stoll can be spotted next to him.

For those struck by the randomness of that duo appearing in a Swift video, you clearly don't know the lore.

So let's get into it.

The Staffords are friends with the 14-time Grammy Award winner and her husband, Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, as are Stoll and his wife, Erin Andrews. The couples attended the Madison Square Garden wedding of Swift and Kelce this summer alongside Charissa Thompson and her significant other, Steven Cundari -- the latter of whom is also featured in the black-tie event scene of Swift's video posing next to Farrell.

As for Andrews and Thompson, the duo have been vocal supporters of Swift and the Kansas City Chiefs star's relationship since before they started dating, even making a plea on their "Calm Down" podcast for the singer to give Kelce a chance. Meanwhile, the Staffords' four daughters are known Swift fans, with Kelly sharing in 2024 that she and Matthew surprised the girls with a trip to see "The Eras Tour" in New Orleans. Kelly and her daughters also attended the June premiere of "Toy Story 5" in Los Angeles where Swift made a surprise appearance to perform her song "I Knew It, I Knew You."

Stafford said his daughters were one of the main reasons he agreed to appear in the video, which he filmed sometime during the offseason.

"They were right there with me," Stafford said. "That's one of the main reasons that I ended up going to do that. She wanted to offer an experience for our family and our kids to see that. I'm obviously really grateful and excited to be in it. My girls, as they do with all her songs, love that song. I was actually driving them to soccer yesterday and they were asking me to play it in the car so we had it on repeat. It's been good."

Stafford also came away impressed by getting an up-close look at Swift's creative process.

"It was cool. It was really cool," Stafford said. "It's cool for me, obviously for Kelly, for us two, but obviously for our kids too. Just to watch her do her thing is pretty impressive. From borderline directing, producing, writing, all of it, editing live as we were doing it. It was really cool to be a part of it. I've never been a part of it before. I probably won't ever be again based on my acting chops, but it was a cool day."

articles.headline: UEFA receives Real Madrid dossier on Barcelona-Negreira case
articles.description: UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.
articles.body:
MADRID -- UEFA has received "a substantial amount of documents" from Real Madrid related to its ongoing inquiry into the Negreira case, European football's governing body said on Thursday.

Payments made by Barcelona to companies linked to José María Enriquez Negreira -- the former vice-president of Spain's Technical Committee of Referees -- over two decades have been subject to a UEFA investigation since 2023, while there is also an ongoing Spanish criminal case.

Barcelona have said the payments, which totaled over €7 million ($7.9m), were made for technical refereeing reports.

- Ronaldo's Portugal walkout is nothing new; he has a long history of rows with coaches

- Source: Mbappé to be available for Clásico

- Raphinha back at Barça, injured in Brazil game

"UEFA can confirm that it has received from Real Madrid CF a substantial amount of documents related to the ongoing investigation into FC Barcelona in the matter involving José María Enríquez Negreira," UEFA confirmed in a statement on Thursday.

"The UEFA Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors have also received these latest documents which they will assess as part of their ongoing review."

Real Madrid said the dossier included "extensive documentation and evidence regarding events of extraordinary seriousness, which directly affect the integrity of the competition and confidence in the refereeing system."

"Real Madrid C.F. considers it essential that, now that UEFA has this documentation, the investigation proceeds with the utmost urgency until its full conclusion, and that the competent bodies take the appropriate decisions in accordance with the severity of the verified facts," the club said.

"Our club will continue to actively collaborate with UEFA and take all actions within its power to clarify events that it deems incompatible with the principles of integrity, transparency, and fair play that should govern European football."

In May, Madrid president Florentino Pérez said that the club was gathering evidence to submit a dossier to UEFA.

Having previously adopted a conciliatory tone with Barcelona -- saying in 2024 that the two clubs "have to help each other" as they worked together on the proposed European Super League -- Pérez has since been extremely critical of his LaLiga rivals.

"They've stolen seven league [titles] from me," Pérez said in May.

In a statement, Barcelona emphasized that Thursday's development did not equate to "any new proceedings."

"The proceedings were initiated in 2023, with the appointment of two investigators who have since carried out the action they deemed appropriate," Barcelona said. "The Club has always complied with all their requests. These proceedings have not been reopened because they have never been closed.

articles.headline: Downing Street clarifies Andy Burnham's remarks on Man City case
articles.description: A spokesperson for Andy Burnham has insisted the guilty verdict against Manchester City is "serious" after remarks the Prime Minister made about the case on Wednesday raised eyebrows.
articles.body:
A spokesperson for Andy Burnham has insisted the guilty verdict against Manchester City is "serious" after remarks the Prime Minister made about the case on Wednesday raised eyebrows.

Burnham told the BBC on Wednesday he would be "really concerned" if City's Abu Dhabi owners sold the club in the wake of City being found to have breached the Premier League's financial rules by an independent commission, crediting them with being "a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester."

Burnham also appeared to draw parallels between City's guilty verdict and the handling of a disciplinary case against Everton, the club he supports.

He said he still held the view very firmly that the Toffees were "not fairly treated" and added: "I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled.

"So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming Prime Minister."

Burnham's comments have drawn criticism on social media and shadow sports minister Louie French called for the Government to "keep politics out of football," with the case set to proceed to an appeal board and a sanctions hearing.

A No. 10 Downing Street spokesman said on Thursday: "As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

"If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

- Klopp not preparing for more titles after verdict against Man City

- Man City owners must sell due to 'shame of their guilt' - Jamie Carragher

Meanwhile, a parliamentary select committee wants answers from the permanent secretary of Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC) regarding any tax implications of the City case.

The chair of the Treasury Committee, Dame Meg Hillier, has written to JP Marks asking whether he is aware of the commission's findings, in particular what it said about the use of "sham" arrangements to conceal liabilities to staff.

Hillier also asked Marks whether he had asked for an unredacted copy of the decision published on Tuesday.

"While I acknowledge that taxpayer confidentiality may inhibit what you can disclose, I would welcome reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case," Hillier wrote.

City are expected to lodge an appeal against the guilty verdict before Friday's deadline, having claimed the commission's decision contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe".
